# Article Outline Template

> Copy this into a new document, fill it in, then paste it into the Studio.
> Delete any line that does not apply. Do not leave a heading with nothing under
> it — remove the heading instead.
> Every claim that needs a source must end up in the **References** section at
> the bottom. If you cannot point to a source for a sentence, rewrite the
> sentence to be more modest.

## 5. Nigerian context check

> An article without a Nigerian example is not finished.

- [ ] At least one real Nigerian food, meal or market scenario
- [ ] Amounts are in units a Nigerian reader recognises (a cup of garri, a
      bunch of ugu, one medium-sized fruit)
- [ ] Examples are affordable, not aspirational
- [ ] If the topic only applies to a region, say so

**The example I will use:** _______________________________________

---

## 6. Language check

- [ ] British spelling: colour, organisation, programme, fibre
- [ ] Short sentences. Long ones are hard for a tired reader.
- [ ] No sentence over about 25 words
- [ ] Every technical word is explained the first time it appears
- [ ] Reads out loud sensibly (test it)
- [ ] No marketing language: *game-changing, revolutionary, miracle, ultimate,
      guaranteed, secret, breakthrough, detox, cure, heals, treats, prevents*

**Search your draft for these before submitting:** cure · treat · heal · prevent
· guarantee · detox · miracle · best · everyone · always

---

## 7. References

> At least one. The Studio will not let you publish without it. For every
> claim that could be questioned, there should be a source that actually
> supports that specific claim.

**Where to look, in order of preference:**

1. World Health Organization (who.int)
2. Nigeria's Federal Ministry of Health, or NPHCDA / NBS / UNICEF Nigeria
3. Food and Agriculture Organization (fao.org)
4. United Nations Children's Fund (unicef.org)
5. Peer-reviewed systematic reviews
6. Recognised professional nutrition or medical bodies
7. Nigerian studies, where the local context genuinely matters

**Do not use as the main evidence:** personal blogs, news articles quoting
somebody else, social media posts, commercial supplement or product pages, or
any site selling the thing it is recommending.

| # | Title | Publisher | URL | Date you read it |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | | | | |
| 2 | | | | |
| 3 | | | | |

## 9. Final pre-submission check

- [ ] Title under 80 characters
- [ ] Summary under 300 characters and stands alone
- [ ] At least 2 key takeaways
- [ ] Every heading level in order, nothing skipped
- [ ] At least one Nigerian, affordable example
- [ ] At least one reference, and I have read it and it says what I claim
- [ ] No cure / treat / heal / prevent / guarantee language
- [ ] I have told a reader when to see a professional
- [ ] I have searched for the prohibited words
- [ ] No statement about a child's or a woman's individual medical result
- [ ] Image consent recorded, or the image removed
- [ ] Read out loud, sentence by sentence
- [ ] Someone who is not a nutritionist could understand it
- [ ] Review Status set to **Submitted for Review**
- [ ] Reviewer has actually been told
